reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes depositing money into the OneCoin-related scheme in exchange for a promised doubling of accounts, using a time-limited deadline and urging viewers to contact the group. The speaker presents the deposit and payment certificate as the route to receiving the duplicated accounts, rather than reporting or criticizing the offer.

citations.quote: all those who make their deposits before the end of the month and have their payment certificate
they will have the additional double of the bank accounts
So make sure to contact us so that those people can make their deposits
Notice to all Onecoin members only two days to double everyone

opening.argument: The speaker presents this as a relayed internal update, not as a personal guarantee or independently verified financial promise. He expressly attributes the information to another person, saying, "We just had a word from Dr. Rucha," and addresses "all the people in the team." That attribution matters: the clip can be understood as passing along a reported policy whose details viewers would need to assess, rather than certifying that the outcome is certain. The supplied speech contains no personal claim of authority, no assurance that deposits are safe, and no statement that every participant will profit. The reference interpretation therefore reads promotional certainty into a short, attributed announcement.

citations.quote: We just had a word from Dr. Rucha
Hello to all the people in the team

rebuttal.rebuttal: The quoted deposit language shows what the reported policy allegedly required, but it does not establish that the speaker personally verified or guaranteed the result. The attribution to Dr. Rucha is omitted from the prosecution's characterization, even though it supplies important context. Likewise, the title's deadline language conflicts with the spoken reference to the end of the month and 30 days in September, weakening its reliability as proof of a deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: We just had a word from Dr. Rucha
before the end of the month
during those 30 days in September

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Attribution does not turn the message into a warning or remove its operative promise. The speaker repeats that people who deposit will receive duplicated accounts and then tells the group to contact him so they can make deposits. Calling this a reported policy does not qualify the outcome; it relays the inducement and encourages action. The title's timing is not necessary to establish the solicitation because the spoken message independently supplies the deposit requirement and doubling benefit.

citations.quote: they will have the additional double of the bank accounts
So make sure to contact us so that those people can make their deposits

opening.argument: The content is more plausibly a news-style update to an existing team than a tutorial teaching viewers how to invest. The speaker opens by addressing "all the people in the team," says there was a new piece of information from Dr. Rucha, and frames the message as something to pass through "all the people in the group." That structure is consistent with relaying organizational news or discussing a program's stated terms. No demonstration, account screen, payment interface, instructional steps, or proof of a completed return appears in the supplied record. The evidence supports discussion of an alleged change, but does not establish that this video itself executes or verifies a financial transaction.

citations.quote: Hello to all the people in the team
We just had a word from Dr. Rucha
let's give this message to all the people in the group

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side assumes that mentioning a deposit makes the clip a solicitation, but a news update can accurately report what a program requires without independently certifying it. The speaker's organizational framing and attribution are not addressed. Nor does the record show a tutorial, transaction, or demonstrated result; it shows a verbal announcement whose subject is the program's stated account treatment.

citations.quote: Hello to all the people in the team
We just had a word from Dr. Rucha

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not merely descriptive reporting. The speaker does not explain or scrutinize the alleged policy; he tells recipients to spread it and to contact him so deposits can be made. The absence of a payment interface or completed transaction is immaterial because promotional solicitation can occur through speech alone. The team framing identifies the intended audience, while the action request identifies the video's practical purpose.

citations.quote: let's give this message to all the people in the group
So make sure to contact us so that those people can make their deposits

opening.argument: The supplied record does not establish the mechanism needed to classify this as a scam rather than promotion of an external membership or financial service. It does not identify a payment channel, account credentials, fee, contract, withdrawal process, recruiting commission, or actual transfer of funds. The description only says to join a financial future by contacting the promoters, without supplying the destination or method. Even the spoken account language does not show where deposits go or how duplication would technically occur. At most, the clip advertises a stated benefit to members and directs interested people to make contact; the missing operational details leave the alleged scam mechanism unproven.

citations.quote: join the financial future by contacting us through ...
all those who make their deposits before the end of the month and have their payment certificate
they will have the additional double of the bank accounts

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution supplies the conclusion that the benefit is an investment return, but the record does not show a financial instrument, transfer destination, or payment procedure. It also does not establish downline income, credential collection, or a completed transaction. The title and description provide promotional context, yet they do not fill those evidentiary gaps or prove that the promised account treatment was deceptive.

citations.quote: join the financial future by contacting us through ...
have their payment certificate

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam classification does not require showing a bank interface, credentials, or a completed transfer. The mechanism is stated plainly: make a deposit by a deadline, possess a payment certificate, and receive duplicated accounts. The speaker then directs people to contact the group so they can deposit. Missing technical details do not convert an explicit deposit-for-doubling proposition into ordinary commerce; they simply leave the operational mechanics unstated.
